name: FAO e-Agriculture homepage: community of practice and 2026 challenge news
title: FAO e-Agriculture homepage: community of practice and 2026 challenge news
answer: The FAO e-Agriculture homepage is a United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization landing page for a global community of practice on information and communication technologies for sustainable agriculture and rural development. Its most useful content is the description of e-Agriculture as a WSIS Action Line C7 initiative facilitated by FAO, plus news that the Global AgriInno Challenge 2026 selected 13 youth led solutions from 137 valid applications out of 191 total. The page does not contain the benchmarking index, platform adoption metrics, or yield and income impact claims attributed to this source.

sections.body: The source is the e-Agriculture homepage published by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. It is a landing page and community site, harvested on 26 September 2026, rather than a report or dataset. Its stated scope is dialogue and information exchange on information and communication technologies and digital innovations for sustainable agriculture, forestry, fisheries, natural resource management and rural development. It also carries news items, including the Global AgriInno Challenge 2026 and a WSIS Forum description. No author byline or publication date for the page itself is given.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page describes e-Agriculture as a global community of practice that facilitates dialogue, information exchange and sharing of ideas on information and communication technologies for sustainable agriculture and rural development. Its mission is to facilitate discussion on the adoption and use of information and communication technologies and digital innovations in agriculture, forestry, fisheries, natural resource management and rural development. The text says e-Agriculture was born out of Action Line C7 ICT Applications: e-agriculture from the World Summit on the Information Society. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations was assigned as facilitator of this action line and also took up facilitation of the e-Agriculture Community of Practice. It also describes the WSIS Forum as a multistakeholder platform launched in Geneva 2003 and Tunis 2005. News items report that the Global AgriInno Challenge 2026 completed its first stage, with 13 youth led innovation solutions selected from 137 valid applications out of 191 applications in total. Three youth led initiatives tackling pressures facing climate vulnerable food and agriculture systems were named winners at a final pitch event held in Hangzhou, China, on 10 September 2026: AgriKonnekt of Kenya, Berikanpreneur of Indonesia and a third name cut off in the harvested text. A separate item describes farmers in Maiwand district, Kandahar province, using greenhouse cultivation and drip irrigation to grow vegetables while making more efficient use of scarce water resources, with Tela Mohammad among farmers managing a 400 square metre greenhouse shared with five other farmers.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that the Global AgriInno Challenge 2026 selected 13 youth led solutions from 137 valid applications out of 191 applications in total. It states that the final pitch event was held in Hangzhou, China, on 10 September 2026, and names AgriKonnekt of Kenya and Berikanpreneur of Indonesia as winners, with a third name cut off. It states that the WSIS Forum was launched through the Geneva 2003 and Tunis 2005 phases. It states that Tela Mohammad is among farmers managing a 400 square metre greenhouse shared with five other farmers in Maiwand district, Kandahar province. It defines e-Agriculture as a global community of practice and as born out of Action Line C7 ICT Applications: e-agriculture from the World Summit on the Information Society. The text gives no figures on platform adoption, yield or income impact, or a benchmarking index.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in Agriculture would use this source to understand how the Food and Agriculture Organization frames digital innovation through its e-Agriculture community of practice, and to see current youth led agri innovation activity through the Global AgriInno Challenge 2026. It is useful as a pointer to FAO community and event work on information and communication technologies in agriculture. It is not useful for benchmarking platform adoption or yield and income impact, because the harvested text contains no such data or index. It also does not discuss artificial intelligence as a named technology, so it offers context rather than AI specific evidence.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Agriculture

sections.body: This is a homepage with short news excerpts and community description, not a research report, dataset or methodology. Several items are truncated, including the third winner and the greenhouse story. It does not cover artificial intelligence specifically, and it does not contain the benchmarking index, platform adoption metrics, or yield and income impact claims attributed to this source. It is current to the harvest date of 26 September 2026 and includes events dated 2026, but it is partial and may be updated. It is published by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, so it is institutional rather than independent.
